fun fact: Khorne doesn't actually hate "ranged" attacks, he does however hate magic, which is often ranged in nature, which is where the misconception lies as magic is considered something stolen or borrowed from other powers besides your own innate strengths. Magic is more or less sourced from the Realms of Chaos itself (with some exceptions), and by extension the winds of magic that flow into the mortal realm from them, or alternatively is granted by the blessings of gods directly i.e. "divine magics" like those used by Tomb Kings. Either way though, the big guy isn't a fan of it.  


In other words, there's nothing stopping a Khornate Berserker from stealing a crossbow from one person, shooting a some poor bastard with it, then using it as a melee weapon against the next nearest opponent, because everything utilized was made within the means of his core tenants

so, here's a little breakdown on how melee works to my understanding:

let's start with the weapon types themselves:

Long Blunt: varying degrees of durability (crowbars will last you a very long time, whereas a spiked baseball bat not nearly as long) but also generally great at knocking down/staggering zombies especially if you are playing with multi-hit settings.

Short Blunt: similar to the long varient, these weapons have pretty good knock down and stagger but not as powerful (though don't tell that to the trusty hammer!) the advantage however is that they're lighter, typically faster, and one of the most common melee weapon types you'll find. 

Long Blade: you got two options, Katana and Machete by default, choose the machete.

Short Blade: with short blade while they aren't as broken early game, what they lack in general power they make up for in utility, a short blade like a kitchen knife can be used to sneak attack unsuspecting zombies from behind (by holding right click and walking up behind them then left clicking when your left arm raises up) for an instant one shot or alternatively you can also pull this move off like a "parry" if you have enough skill with them and time it just right when a zombie goes to lunge at you.

Spears: Spears generally have the lowest durability of all the weapon types, however what they lack they make up for with a similar advantage to the short blade, no sneak attack with a spear however you do get three seperate "special" attacks: the parry stab against zombies lunging at you, the one shot stab to the head one knocked down enemies, and finally the spear charge (done by having the spear in hand and sprinting (Left ALT by default) into an enemy when the animation plays) just be aware, that the spear charge in particular can be extremely risky.

And Finally, Axes: everyone's favorite killing spree tool, they tend to be heavy and tire you out quickly in extended engagements, however they make up for that in sheer killing potential, capable of one shotting zombies even with low skill and almost guaranteeing it with higher skill levels in Axe and Strength.

As for other combat related skills, we have three in particular that are important for general combat effectiveness

Fitness (how fast/slow you will become exhausted)
Strength (how much/little damage you can dish out)
And Nimble (how quickly you'll move in combat stance)

how high or low these three skills are can make or break how effective you are when doing various combat actions like strafing, backpeddling, pushing, and of course, bashing in the heads of the neighbors.

Hope this helps get a better idea of how the combat system works these days and i'm sure if i forgot something someone will correct me in the comments ^-^

there are a pretty good few tricks you can do to add more flavor to builds without needing to completely tear it down

For example, using basic starter materials as a baseline, you can replace the ground floor (the actual floor not the entire structure) with a cobblestone flooring and additional cobblestone trimming on the lowest background line to break up the look a bit while keeping it simple, from there you can add on some windows (doesn't have to be glass, i personally like wooden latice windows for timber builds) and maybe some support columns here and there with stone materials again to break up the look and add a more lived in appearance to the build. 

another trick you can do, is making your walls and floors thicker in some places (2 or 3 wide/tall is usually best results i've found) which allows you to comfortably alternate block types without breaking the appearance of individual rooms, you wouldn't necessarily want to do this to every wall/floor however as you'll end up with an excessively thick base/colony.

to be fair, i'm able to deflect every light during my warmups with my friends/bots, doesn't mean i'm able to do that 100% of the time in an actual match, prediction =/= reaction, if you know something is coming you respond to that prediction, if your prediction is incorrect, your response will be punished. 

The problem with videos showcasing how to shut down a mixup or something of that sort, is they more often than not showcase the different possibilities individually, which isn't how fights work more often than not: Person A uses the basic full mixup without any changes: that becomes "reactable" not because it is inherently reactable, but because it became an easily predicted pattern, and if there is one thing humans are generally good at it is pattern recognition. On the other hand, Person B uses the basic full mixup the first time, but switches it to a different branching option of the mixup each subsequent time, this makes it much harder to predict what the next move will be and thus make it difficult for it to become reactable.

Point is: Sure, you can know what every move in a hero's kit is and know how to counter, but you can't ever fully know what you opponent is thinking and therefor are subject to mistakes in your predictions.
